- Speech & Thought: Normal rate and flow; logical, goal-directed

Formulation:
Predisposing: None identified  
Precipitating: Acute viral illness; increased year-end workload  
Perpetuating: Limited – symptoms expected to resolve; no maladaptive coping noted  
Protective: Positive work engagement; good insight; no psychiatric history; supportive GP follow-up available

Mental Health Care Plan Details
(Primary clinical focus is reassurance and monitoring rather than formal psychological intervention.)

Principal Problem: No current mental health disorder
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain good mental health; recover from viral illness
- Clinical Goal(s): Monitor for emergence of mood or anxiety symptoms during recovery
- Actions (Patient): Rest, adhere to medical advice, seek GP review if mood changes
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide psycho-education on stress management; invite patient to return if psychological concerns arise

Secondary Problem: Mild situational work stress
- Patient Goal(s): Manage workload without negative impact on well-being
- Clinical Goal(s): Prevent escalation to anxiety or burnout
- Actions (Patient): Implement pacing and breaks; consider brief leave while unwell
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Offer resources on stress management; assess need for referral if stress increases

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Normal stress responses; when to seek help for mood/anxiety; red-flag physical symptoms warranting earlier review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent low mood, loss of interest, significant anxiety, sleep disturbance beyond illness recovery
- Coping Strategies: Rest, hydration, pacing workload, social support

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: To be scheduled if psychological symptoms emerge or at next GP follow-up (1–2 weeks if physical symptoms persist)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
None – DDx list focuses on physical (infective) conditions; no mental health differentials applicable to current presentation.

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: exact patient identifiers, GP details, formal mental health diagnosis, documented consent, review date.  
● Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None; both sources align that no mental health disorder is present.  
● Transcript quality notes: Good quality; primarily physical-health consultation with minimal mental health content.
